$comment: What the unattended runners are allowed to leave unexecuted.
Bashar, 2026-09-07: «I want the unattended overnight runner to tell the truth about platform
quality and coverage. A skipped or unexecuted workflow should never look like a passed
Every number here is a CEILING that a run must stay under, and lowering one is the point:
a budget that is never tightened decays in the direction of hiding things, which is the
failure mode `.claude/CLAUDE.md` names for exemption lists. So the guards also fail when a
budget sits far ABOVE what actually happens — a ceiling of forty over five real skips is
thirty-five future skips nobody will ever be told about.
Raising a number is a reviewed change with a reason in the commit message. That is the
whole mechanism: the skip stops being a footnote in a log and becomes a line in a diff.

why: Zero, and it is achievable today: the entire suite passes with the database available.
It was 1,724 skipped tests across 128 files — 44% of the suite — because `pnpm test` did
not source `.env` and each integration file carries its own
`DATABASE_URL ? describe : describe.skip`. `pnpm verify` printed «2164 passed» and exited
0 while nearly half of it had not run, and that is the gate this project requires before
every commit to `main`.
Measured 2026-09-07: 3,888 passed in 30.58s with the database, against 19.74s without it.
Eleven seconds bought 44% of the coverage back.
`minTests` catches the other direction — a file that stops being COLLECTED at all, by a
rename, a bad glob or an exclude. Nothing skips, nothing fails, and the total quietly
drops. Lowering it is deliberate: tests are sometimes rightly deleted, and then this line
is where that is recorded.
Browser skips are not all the same thing, so they are counted in two ways.
A DECLARED skip states its reason — `test.skip(condition, 'why')` — and several here
legitimately depend on fixture state: an empty media bucket, a listing with no photographs,
a coupon awaiting nobody's decision. Those have a ceiling.
An UNDECLARED skip has no reason attached, which is the dangerous kind: it is
indistinguishable in a summary from a test that ran. `maxUndeclared` is zero. Note what it
catches in practice — Playwright's serial mode skips the rest of a block when one test fails,
with no annotation, so an undeclared skip is usually the SHADOW of a failure.
`maxSlack` stops the ceilings decaying. If real skips fall well below the budget the guard
fails and asks for the number to be lowered, so the ceiling keeps describing the suite rather
than describing history. It did that on its own first run: provisional ceilings of 20 and 12
were 12 and 11 too loose, and the run failed saying so.
MEASURED 2026-09-07 on the one fully green run — the database as it stood, no reset:
chromium 387 passed / 8 skipped of 395, signed-in 108 passed / 1 skipped of 109, nothing
failed and nothing went unrun. These ceilings are those numbers, so a tenth skip is a
decision somebody makes in a diff.
KNOWN TO BE EXCEEDED on a freshly reset testbed, and that is the runner telling the truth
rather than a number needing adjustment. `db:testbed` produces a database on which chromium
skips 21 and three payout and employee specs FAIL — the payout ones because accrual is an
hourly job the reset does not run, which `payout-accounts.spec.ts` says in its own failure
message. Raising these to match would declare that regression acceptable. See §7 of
docs/FUTURE-WORK.md for what has to happen before the reset can be the default.
